key_path: `vercel signup` (new account) or `vercel login` (existing): OAuth 2.0 Device Flow; human approves in browser with Google / GitHub / Apple / ChatGPT / email
if signup was by email: verify email (magic link/OTP)
CLI session token is now usable for the CLI and `vercel api`; for a standalone bearer token: dashboard > Account Settings > Tokens > create scoped token (team scope + expiry)
MCP: `npx -y add-mcp https://mcp.vercel.com -g` or `vercel mcp --clients "Claude Code"`, then OAuth consent in browser
human_gates: email_verification (only for email signup; OAuth signup skips it)
browser consent for device flow / MCP OAuth

agent_native_auth.cli_device_flow: yes: `vercel login` moved to the OAuth 2.0 Device Flow (changelog 2025-09-12); the old email/--github/--oob methods were removed 2026-02-26. `vercel signup` creates an account from the CLI
agent_native_auth.mcp_oauth_dcr: partial: the AS metadata publishes registration_endpoint https://vercel.com/api/login/oauth/register, but docs say Vercel MCP 'only supports AI clients that have been reviewed and approved by Vercel' (client review form). Custom or unknown agents are blocked
agent_native_auth.provisioning_api_mints_keys: no public API documented for minting PATs. Tokens are created in the dashboard. Vercel Connect/OAuth exists for integrations
agent_native_auth.scoped_tokens: yes: access tokens scoped to a team with expiration
agent_native_auth.claimable_anonymous: yes for platforms: Claim Deployments. An agent deploys under its own team, then POST /projects/:id/transfer-request returns a 24h code and the claim URL vercel.com/claim-deployment?code=... The agent operator still needs its own Vercel account, so a solo agent cannot deploy anonymously

remote.auth: OAuth (approved clients only); some public docs-search tools work without auth

mcp.local: none official; stdio clients use `npx mcp-remote https://mcp.vercel.com`
mcp.type: product + docs (search docs, manage projects and deployments, logs, Web Analytics, deploy code, purchases)
mcp.one_click: Cursor deeplink, VS Code `vscode:mcp/install`, Goose deeplink, Devin marketplace, `npx add-mcp` installs into all detected agents, `vercel mcp --clients`

docs_for_agents.markdown_pages: yes: append .md, plus .graph.md cross-link maps with a 'For AI agents' block on every docs page
docs_for_agents.use_with_ai_page: https://vercel.com/get-started.md is an agent-executable onboarding playbook; /docs/agent-resources
docs_for_agents.agent_skills_plugin: `npx plugins add vercel/vercel-plugin`; `npx skills add vercel-labs/agent-skills`

score_justification: CLI signup + device flow, add-mcp installer and an agent-executable get-started.md make the path almost all agent-run. The only human step is one browser approval. Point lost because MCP is allow-listed to approved clients and solo agents have no anonymous deploy.
best_practice: get-started.md: a playbook written for the agent to execute ('Perform actions yourself... Pause only for user authentication'), plus `vercel signup` so the agent can start account creation itself
biggest_gap: MCP OAuth is limited to Vercel-approved clients even though DCR exists, so custom agents and new clients are locked out. Claim Deployments needs the agent operator's own account
